review_scope.review_basis: Frozen claims plus the pinned Q2 full-horizon compatibility summary; no new experiment was executed.
not_reviewed: formal claims, manuscript, and Figure Contracts
new solver runs or external literature

model_interface.input: Workload trace is aggregated into 18 hourly bottom series: 6 source regions x 3 task types, with GPU.h = GPU_Demand x EstimatedDuration_min / 60.
model_interface.forecast_output: A 24-hour nonnegative forecast for all bottom series, with hierarchy-consistent region, type, and system totals and a nominal 95% normalized pooled split-conformal interval.
model_interface.schedule_output: A minute-level, single-execution-region schedule for the actual final-window arrivals. Forecast values are not silently converted into synthetic tasks; the schedule uses actual arrivals and separately carries historical unfinished work.
model_interface.interface_assessment: The separation is auditable and avoids forecast leakage, but the current evidence does not establish an uncertainty-aware end-to-end forecast-to-schedule gain. Treat forecast and dispatch as two linked modules, not as a proven closed-loop optimizer.

algorithm_assessment.baseline: Seasonal naive with lag selected from 24 h and 168 h by four training-only rolling 24 h folds.
algorithm_assessment.main_forecast: Shared HistGradientBoosting residual model over lag 1, 2, 3, 24, 48, and 168 h, 24/168 h rolling statistics, cyclic hour/weekday terms, and region/task-type indicators; residuals are scaled and nonnegative-clipped.
algorithm_assessment.hierarchy: Nonnegative diagonal-WLS reconciliation over 18 bottom series and region/type/system totals; the returned bottom vector defines all aggregate nodes, so coherence is a structural output property.
algorithm_assessment.interval: Normalized pooled split conformal with alpha=0.05, calibrated only on the validation window (432 bottom-series-hour scores), then reported on the untouched 2376--2399 blind window.
algorithm_assessment.scheduling: Historical event-boundary warm-up creates carry-in; a deterministic minute-level CP-SAT assigns each final task exactly once under release, real-time-at-arrival, latency, GPU, IT, facility-power, nonpreemption, and 2406 closeout constraints.
algorithm_assessment.objective: CP-SAT minimizes 100 x waiting minutes plus route latency for the final-window tasks. Energy and carbon are constraint/audit quantities here, not optimized quantities.

evidence_boundaries: WAPE is pooled/system-level evidence; it does not imply improvement for every region-task series.
94.68% is empirical pooled coverage on the blind window, not an exact or conditional 95% guarantee.
FEASIBLE and the recorded gap must be reported; the 538-task solution is not proven globally optimal.

baseline_comparability.forecast: Pass: same horizon, same rolling origins, same training/validation/blind split, and comparable forecast/interval fields for the seasonal baseline and main model.
baseline_comparability.scheduling: Pass: FIFO/local-first uses the same actual arrivals, carry-in, candidate regions, resource mappings, horizon, hard constraints, and output schema; both schedules receive an independent audit.
baseline_comparability.remaining_caveat: The forecast baseline and scheduling baseline are valid module-level controls, but no frozen evidence compares a schedule driven by forecast intervals against a schedule driven by point forecasts.

reproducibility: Fixed seed 20260801 and pinned Python/scikit-learn/OR-Tools environments are recorded in the Q1 run manifests.
Training-only rolling selection, nonnegative forecasts, hierarchy coherence, carry-in conservation, hard audits, solver status, and fallback trigger are recorded as machine-checkable artifacts.
risk_probes: Time leakage was checked by excluding 2376--2399 from lag/shrinkage selection and calibration inputs.
Carry-in conservation and unresolved historical-task checks passed; no silent deletion is allowed.
GPU, IT, facility-power, network-latency, and 2406 boundary checks passed for both main and FIFO schedules.
The only fallback is a 6 h rolling/12 h lookahead CP-SAT path; it is a smoke-tested contract and was not substituted into the main result.
Sparse series can show unstable WAPE and groupwise coverage even when pooled metrics are acceptable; this is a modeling risk, not a failed hard audit.

innovation_and_gain.verifiable_gain: The defensible contribution is the auditable composition of hierarchical residual forecasting, nonnegative reconciliation, pooled conformal uncertainty, and constraint-audited dispatch. The blind pooled WAPE and feasible schedule are real-data gains within their stated scopes.
innovation_and_gain.innovation_boundary: The current evidence does not prove a novel forecasting theorem, a probabilistic conditional-coverage guarantee, or an end-to-end dispatch improvement caused by the interval. Any novelty language should emphasize the reproducible interface and audit design rather than claim optimality or causality.

findings.title: Pooled forecast evidence must not be generalized to every sparse series
findings.impact: Macro and bottom-level behavior can differ substantially from the pooled WAPE; series-level claims would overstate the evidence.
findings.action: Report pooled WAPE/RMSE with per-series diagnostics in a supporting table or figure and state the sparse-series limitation.

findings.title: Conformal coverage is pooled empirical coverage
findings.impact: Pooling 432 calibration scores supports a marginal diagnostic over cells, not exact 95% coverage for each region-task or horizon.
findings.action: Use nominal/empirical wording and test groupwise calibration only as a conditional follow-up.

findings.title: The CP-SAT main run is feasible with a nonzero gap
findings.impact: Calling it optimal would be false and would invalidate the algorithm description.
findings.action: Keep FEASIBLE plus the recorded 3.515% gap; optionally run a bounded time-extension experiment before freezing any stronger scheduling statement.

findings.title: Forecast uncertainty is not yet an operational reserve rule
findings.impact: The current Q1 result supports two auditable modules, not a measured benefit from feeding conformal upper bounds into scheduling.
findings.action: If an end-to-end innovation is needed, run the conditional reserve experiment below and freeze it only after a same-input baseline comparison.

findings.title: Metric names should distinguish pooled errors from workload-weighted WAPE
findings.impact: The pooled MAE/RMSE fields are aggregated over cells; only WAPE uses total absolute actual workload as its denominator. Calling all of them system-weighted would be ambiguous.
findings.action: Define pooled MAE/RMSE and workload-normalized WAPE separately in tables, captions, and the metric dictionary.

model_interface.input: All 50000 actual arrivals in hours 0--2399 plus supplied hourly price, carbon intensity, renewable availability, static latency, capacity, PUE, and power mappings; hours 2400--2405 are closeout only.
model_interface.decision_variables: Each non-real-time task may exchange its execution region and start minute within a bounded 72 h option horizon; real-time reservations remain fixed and each task remains nonpreemptive in one region.
model_interface.rolling_rule: Process six-hour release blocks, start from a complete feasible FIFO/local-first incumbent, evaluate at most eight coarse start options per eligible region plus earliest/old starts, and accept only feasible exchanges that strictly improve the score and reduce cost or carbon.
model_interface.score: score = 1.0 x marginal_cost/1000 + 4.0 x marginal_carbon + 0.015 x wait_min + 0.015 x latency_ms - 0.05 x renewable_MWh; these are fixed policy weights, not learned dual variables.

objective_and_constraints.scope_boundary: Q2 does not optimize storage state or grid exchange; those decisions remain Q3/Q4 interfaces. Static latency excludes congestion, migration energy, and migration fees because they are not supplied in the problem.

evidence_summary.robustness_scope: Six operation blocks have zero supplied-input SLA violation; fixed-schedule -5% GPU/IT probes expose headroom sensitivity and are not rescheduled feasibility results.

baseline_comparability.baseline: Full-horizon FIFO latency-feasible local-first schedule with identical task rows, capacity audits, cost/carbon/latency/renewable definitions, and closeout boundary.
baseline_comparability.interpretation: The deltas are a same-input deterministic policy comparison, not a causal estimate and not proof that the candidate dominates FIFO on every metric.

reproducibility: Fixed seed 20260801, pinned Python/numpy/pandas environment, command, code/data hashes, runtime, and metric units are recorded in the Q2 run manifest.
The second complete exchange replay reproduced the same task-region-start schedule, supporting implementation determinism for the pinned input.
risk_probes: Latency-limit-minus-10% fixed-schedule probes passed for both methods, but this is exposure only.
GPU-capacity-minus-5% fixed-schedule probes failed for both methods (candidate has more exposed region-minutes); this does not invalidate supplied-capacity feasibility.
IT-capacity-minus-5% fixed-schedule probes failed for both methods and identify headroom sensitivity.
Renewable-availability-minus-20% is a metric-only scenario; it does not re-solve capacity or task feasibility.
Minute exact-scan fallback for unresolved flexible tasks was not triggered; no fallback performance claim is allowed.

innovation_and_gain.verifiable_gain: A practical auditable combination of fixed real-time reservations, bounded rolling exchanges, minute-level feasibility checks, and same-input FIFO control reduces the reported cost and carbon while preserving all supplied-input hard audits.
innovation_and_gain.innovation_boundary: The implementation is a deterministic one-pass heuristic over a bounded option set. The name lagrangian_balanced describes a weighted score, but no multiplier-update or dual-convergence proof is present; describe it as a Lagrangian-style weighted exchange unless an adaptive-dual experiment is actually run.

findings.title: Bounded exchange is not a global or MILP optimum
findings.impact: A full-horizon cumulative improvement can coexist with a jointly better multi-task assignment outside the eight-option local search.
findings.action: Use deterministic rolling exchange heuristic wording and retain the 72 h/8-option boundary in the method and figure captions.

findings.title: Fixed score weights need sensitivity evidence before being called selected weights
findings.impact: Cost, carbon, wait, latency, and renewable terms have different units and are not normalized by an adaptive dual scheme; small weight changes may alter the policy.
findings.action: Run the pre-registered policy grid and report a feasible Pareto table or retain the weights as a declared policy choice.

findings.title: Capacity stress probes are fixed-schedule exposure tests
findings.impact: They cannot support a claim of robustness to reduced capacity because no rescheduling was performed under the perturbation.
findings.action: Re-solve candidate and FIFO under the same perturbations before using robustness language.

findings.title: Full-horizon replay is not the same as an online information experiment
findings.impact: The supplied-input run reads all arrivals, so it should not be described as deployment-ready online control without an information-availability check.
findings.action: Use offline deterministic replay wording or run the online-hidden-future ablation.

findings.title: The improvement is a trade-off
findings.impact: Candidate latency rises by 4.18976 ms and renewable utilization is slightly lower even though cost and carbon improve.
findings.action: Report the vector of metrics and do not claim uniform dominance over FIFO.

findings.title: Avoid calling initial cross-region placement migration
findings.impact: The model enforces one-region nonpreemptive execution and forbids mid-task migration; an artifact field named migration_rate can be misread as an illegal task move.
findings.action: Define that field as cross-region placement share (or initial remote assignment rate) and reserve migration terminology for an explicitly modeled transfer event.

recommended_next_experiments.purpose: Check whether pooled conformal intervals hide systematic undercoverage in sparse region-task groups.
recommended_next_experiments.minimal_design: Keep the existing 0--2351 training, 2352--2375 calibration, and 2376--2399 blind windows and the fitted HGBR predictions fixed. Compare pooled calibration with region-by-task-type groupwise calibration using the same normalized score and nonnegative clipping.
recommended_next_experiments.activation_trigger: Run before making any conditional or per-series coverage statement, or if a blind group-coverage audit shows an absolute deviation from 0.95 greater than 0.05.
recommended_next_experiments.acceptance_rule: Adopt groupwise intervals only if pooled WAPE is not worsened by more than 1% relative, pooled coverage remains in the declared diagnostic range, and group coverage moves closer to 0.95 without implausible width inflation; otherwise retain pooled intervals.
recommended_next_experiments.claim_boundary: This experiment can support calibration diagnostics only; it cannot establish finite-sample conditional coverage.

recommended_next_experiments.purpose: Determine whether the feasible Q1 schedule is materially improved by a bounded additional solve budget.
recommended_next_experiments.minimal_design: Repeat the identical final-task, carry-in, seed, objective, and hard-audit pipeline with a 180 s wall limit; record status, objective, bound, gap, runtime, and all audit fields. Keep the 90 s result as the control.
recommended_next_experiments.activation_trigger: Current main status is FEASIBLE with a recorded nonzero gap; activate if stronger optimization wording or a schedule-quality comparison is desired.
recommended_next_experiments.acceptance_rule: Use the extended run only if it remains feasible, all audits pass, and the objective improvement is material under a predeclared tolerance; otherwise keep the 90 s result and its gap wording.
recommended_next_experiments.claim_boundary: Even an improved incumbent is not a global optimum unless the solver proves optimality.

recommended_next_experiments.purpose: Test an end-to-end innovation without changing the frozen point-forecast or schedule claims.
recommended_next_experiments.minimal_design: Use the conformal upper workload bound only to construct a deterministic regional reserve scenario for the next 24 h, then rerun the same CP-SAT model and FIFO control with identical task and resource audits. Do not create synthetic task rows or alter real-time arrival rules.
recommended_next_experiments.activation_trigger: Only if an explicit uncertainty-aware capacity policy is needed and an upper bound exceeds a measured regional headroom threshold.
recommended_next_experiments.acceptance_rule: Keep the reserve policy only when every hard audit passes and the added conservatism has a documented operational benefit; otherwise retain the current modular interface.
recommended_next_experiments.claim_boundary: This would be a scenario analysis, not a guarantee against future demand shocks.

recommended_next_experiments.purpose: Test whether the reported cost/carbon gain is stable to the fixed multi-objective score weights.
recommended_next_experiments.minimal_design: Run a small pre-registered grid varying the carbon-to-cost emphasis (for example 2, 4, and 8 while preserving the same wait/latency/renewable terms), using the same six-hour blocks, 72 h horizon, eight-option cap, seed, baseline, and minute-level audits.
metrics: cost and carbon change vs FIFO
recommended_next_experiments.activation_trigger: Required before describing the current weights as data-selected, robust, or Pareto-efficient; optional if they are explicitly declared policy weights.
recommended_next_experiments.acceptance_rule: Select a policy only from the feasible nondominated set under a stated preference rule; if no stable choice exists, report the full trade-off table and keep the current policy as a transparent reference.
recommended_next_experiments.claim_boundary: A finite grid does not prove global Pareto optimality.

recommended_next_experiments.purpose: Convert the current fixed-schedule headroom probes into genuine robustness evidence.
recommended_next_experiments.minimal_design: Reduce GPU and IT capacities by 5% using the existing stress convention, re-run the candidate exchange and the same FIFO baseline from a feasible or explicitly diagnosed incumbent, and independently audit all minute-level constraints. Keep renewable -20% as a metric-only scenario unless the model is extended to re-solve with renewable limits.
recommended_next_experiments.activation_trigger: Current fixed-schedule GPU and IT probes fail, so activate before claiming resilience to capacity loss.
recommended_next_experiments.acceptance_rule: A robustness claim requires re-solved schedules with no unreported violations and explicit fallback/unscheduled-task accounting; otherwise report only headroom exposure.
recommended_next_experiments.claim_boundary: Perturbations are deterministic sensitivity scenarios, not stochastic reliability probabilities.

recommended_next_experiments.purpose: Separate an offline full-horizon replay from an online policy claim.
recommended_next_experiments.minimal_design: At each six-hour block, hide future task rows and expose only arrivals through the block boundary plus carry-in; preserve the same static price/carbon/renewable inputs and constraints. Run the rolling exchange and FIFO control with identical output schemas.
recommended_next_experiments.activation_trigger: Run before using online, real-time, or deployment-ready wording; otherwise describe the result as a deterministic offline replay.
recommended_next_experiments.acceptance_rule: Only claim online applicability if every block remains auditable and the sign/magnitude of improvements is reported with any degradation; no future information may enter the block decision.
recommended_next_experiments.claim_boundary: This tests information timing, not unseen-distribution generalization.

recommended_next_experiments.purpose: Quantify local heuristic quality without implying a full-horizon exact optimum.
recommended_next_experiments.minimal_design: On one or more fixed 72 h windows and a documented small task subset, solve an exact MILP/CP-SAT model with the same task, latency, resource, and closeout constraints; compare the heuristic incumbent to the exact objective and metric vector.
recommended_next_experiments.activation_trigger: Only if a quantitative local optimality diagnostic is needed for the algorithm discussion.
recommended_next_experiments.acceptance_rule: Use the result as a local-window benchmark; never extrapolate its gap to the 2400 h horizon.
recommended_next_experiments.claim_boundary: The benchmark is window- and subset-specific.

global_rules: Use journal-spectrum-v2 only, one primary plotting area per figure, and a non-color secondary encoding (line style, marker, or hatch).
Read every plotted number from frozen evidence locators; no manually typed endpoint or metric values.
Keep units explicit and do not combine cost, carbon, latency, and renewable utilization on one axis.
Q1: Forecast interval figure: show actual versus reconciled 24 h forecast in GPU.h with the nominal 95% band; caption it as pooled empirical coverage and avoid per-series guarantee wording.

Forecast comparison figure: use one metric family per primary axis (for example pooled WAPE/RMSE or an explicitly separated statistics table) and state that aggregate improvement does not imply universal series improvement.

Schedule feasibility figure: show minute/hour resource occupancy against GPU, IT, and facility limits with carry-in boundary and 2406 closeout marker; annotate CP-SAT FEASIBLE and the recorded gap, never optimal.
If sparse series are shown, prefer small multiples only when complementary evidence cannot be separated; otherwise use a ranked supporting table to avoid unreadable multi-panel decoration.
Q2: The staged cumulative facility-energy cost index comparison is suitable as a single-primary-axes figure: candidate solid/circle, FIFO dashed/square, neutral FIFO=100% reference, and 0--2405 h axis.

Keep carbon, latency, renewable utilization, and fixed-schedule stress probes in separate figures or tables with their own units; do not imply that the cost curve alone proves a multi-objective optimum.
Add the 72 h option horizon, six-hour release blocks, and bounded-heuristic qualifier to the caption or adjacent method text; do not label the line as an optimal policy.
A capacity-headroom chart may be used as sensitivity evidence only if its caption says fixed-schedule exposure unless a rescheduled perturbation is subsequently frozen.

verdict_rationale: Q1 and Q2 have coherent model interfaces, same-class baselines, pinned reproducibility records, and audited supplied-input feasibility. The package is suitable for root-agent integration after preserving the stated boundaries: Q1 forecast gains are pooled diagnostics and CP-SAT is feasible rather than optimal; Q2 is a fixed-weight, bounded deterministic exchange heuristic with latency/renewable trade-offs and fixed-schedule capacity stress failures.
